newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT CRUDE ENDS WEAK ON IRAQI EXPORT NEWS.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT CRUDE ENDS WEAK ON IRAQI EXPORT NEWS.

text.p: IPE Brent crude slid on Wednesday to close just above the day's low after Iraq said it planned to resume oil exports suspended since late May in little more than a week's time.
"The market's been quite choppy but it's basically been going in one direction all day because of Iraq," said a broker.
Sept Brent closed 34 cents lower at $19.18 a barrel, just eight cents above the session low.
Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said on Wednesday Iraq expected to export the full $2 billion worth of oil allowed under the U.N. oil-for-food plan before the December 6 deadline.

The second phase of the deal began on June 8 but Iraq's insistence on a revised aid distribution plan delayed the restart and means exports will have to run flat out to meet the interim $1 billion target set for September 5.
Traders said the prospect of a flood of Iraqi crude exports in the second half of August took its toll on European spot and paper market sentiment which worked through to prompt futures.
The nearby Sept/Oct spread dived to a 10-cent contango from around unchanged on Tuesday.
Approval of Iraq's pricing formulas by the U.N. overseers gave the market another push lower during afternoon dealing. The Security Council has 48 hours to raise any objections.
Earlier, crude found some support from news that a week-long closure of Colombia's main crude oil pipeline after a wave of rebel attacks and a landslide was beginning to disrupt exports.
State oil company Ecopetrol said it declared force majeure on loadings at Covenas on the Caribbean, delaying two cargoes.
A declaration of force majeure by Venezuela's PDVSA on two or three gasoline cargoes due to problems at the Cardon refinery helped lift NYMEX gasoline off early lows.
Earlier, IPE Aug gas oil closed $1 weaker at $175.50 a tonne. --Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
